title: expectrail.repro-score/v1
description: The reproduction rate of one live run on the public reproduction bench: per defect, whether a generated check passed on the clean game 3 times of 3 and failed on the bug build 3 times of 3, read from that run's jit-run records. Every defect runs with the same stand-in candidate, a comment line that changes nothing, so the check comes from the bug build and the report alone. A defect with no usable record is no-result and never counts as reproduced. A miss carries a reason only where the records can show one. Under the pixel setting (#286) a row's counts include its pixel checks, and its pixel object says how many were pixel checks. With a screen record, each row says what it measured, and the totals give the screen-only defects apart. A score counts records of one candidate setting, shown or withheld, and says withheld when it is. Written and read by expectrail.repro.score.

reason.description: The issue's vocabulary (#285, step 2), and undetermined. The scorer assigns budget, flaky, wrong-predicate, no-signal and undetermined from the run's records and the visibility record. route-never-reaches and probe-language only with a screen record, on a row whose visibility is none: route-never-reaches where the row's screen is neither, probe-language where it is screen-only and the offer is not the pixel one. The reader recomputes both, so a record that carries one elsewhere, or undetermined where the screen record gives one, is refused.

benchSha256.description: The bench file the defects were read from.

noFixSha256.description: The stand-in candidate every case ran with.

visibilitySha256.description: The visibility record the rows' visibility came from, or null when none was given.

screenSha256.description: The screen record (expectrail/repro/screen.py) the rows' screen came from. There exactly when every row has screen.

source.description: Where the jit-run records came from, as the person who scored them said: a CI run, for example. Not checked. One line: no control character.

offer.description: What the generator was offered in the records this score counts (expectrail/jit/offer.py). A record made with another setting is a row with no result.

candidate.description: There only when the score counts records made with the candidate withheld (issue #285, step 6: the model was given no byte of the candidate, so every reproducing check came from the report and the bug build alone). Absent, the score counts records made with the candidate shown, as every score did before the setting existed. A record made with the other setting is a row with no result.

visibility.description: What the library probes see of this defect, copied from the visibility record; null when it has no row for it.

why.description: For no-result: why there is no result. One line: no control character.

kept.description: Checks that passed on the clean game 3 of 3 and failed 3 of 3 on a near miss, worked out from the runs.

reproducing.description: The kept checks that failed 3 of 3 on the bug build, with and without the no-fix candidate. The bug build's three fails are read from the check's catch entry in the jit-run record, which keeps those runs. Under the pixel setting, also the kept pixel checks (jit-px-...) that failed 3 of 3 on the bug build with and without the no-fix candidate, read from the record's pixelChecks.

pixel.description: Only in a score made with signals-reach-evidence-pixel, on every row with a record: how many of the row's proposed, kept and reproducing checks are pixel checks (expectrail/jit/pixel.py). Kept is read from the pixel rows' runs, never their status. The reader also holds every reproducing id to the jit-px- prefix.

screen.description: Only when the score was given a screen record: what it measured of this defect (expectrail/repro/screen.py); null when it has no row for it, or its row is an error.

evidence.description: For a miss: what in the records gives the reason. One line: no control character.

traceVisible.description: Defects whose visibility is signal or trace-only: the engine's record differs on some library probe.

pixel.description: Only in a pixel score: pixel checks proposed and kept over all rows, the reproduced defects with a reproducing pixel check, and those whose reproducing checks are all pixel checks.

screenOnly.description: Only with a screen record: defects it measured as screen-only.
